findings.title: Hung/dead flusher processes are never killed before restart because isinstance check fails for SpawnProcess
findings.body: `_ensure_processes_alive` only calls `process.kill()` when `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. The processes are created via `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process`, which is `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess` — a direct subclass of `BaseProcess`, not of `multiprocessing.Process` (`multiprocessing.context.Process`). The isinstance check is therefore always False in production, and `kill()` is never invoked. The previous code called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally (catching ValueError), so this is a regression. Consequence: when a process is deemed hung (`cause == "hang"`), it is left running and a second process is started for the same shards. Two flushers then concurrently call `flush_segments`/`done_flush_segments` on the same Redis shards, producing duplicate segments to Kafka and racing on Redis state, while the stale processes accumulate (up to MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS per index). The same broken check in `join()` (line 346) means `terminate()` is also never called on shutdown. Use `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess)` or `not isinstance(process, threading.Thread)`.

findings.title: Added time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched earlier in the test
findings.body: `test_basic` does `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` at the top, and the new line `time.sleep(0.1)` resolves `time.sleep` at call time through the `time` module, so it calls the patched no-op. The comment says it gives the flusher thread time to process after the drift change, but it waits zero seconds. The race it was meant to fix remains: `step.join()` immediately sets `stopped`, and if the flusher thread observes `stopped` before running `flush_segments` with the new drift, `messages` is empty and `(msg,) = messages` fails. Capture the real sleep before patching (as `test_flusher.py` does with `from time import sleep`) or poll for `messages` with a deadline.

findings.title: join() breaks out of the loop on deadline and skips terminate() for remaining processes
findings.body: In `join()`, when the deadline has passed the loop does `break`, so any processes not yet visited never reach `process.terminate()`. The inner `while` already exits immediately once the deadline has passed, so the `break` is unnecessary and only has the effect of skipping termination of the remaining processes. On a slow shutdown this leaves spawned flusher processes running after the consumer's strategy has been joined (they are daemonic, but will keep flushing until the parent actually exits).

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag keys ('shard' vs 'shards') with a comma-joined multi-shard value
findings.body: `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` are tagged with `{"shard": shard_tag}` while `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` uses `{"shards": shard_tag}`. All three use the same comma-joined string (e.g. "0,4,8"), so the `shard` tag name is misleading and dashboards/queries cannot filter consistently across these metrics. Additionally, `flusher_unhealthy` (line 244) emits one point per individual shard with `shard=<int>`, so the same tag key has different semantics across metrics. Pick one key and one value shape.

findings.title: Redis memory info is fetched once per flusher buffer although all buffers point to the same cluster
findings.body: `submit()` iterates `self.buffers.values()` and calls `get_memory_info()` on each. Every `SpansBuffer` connects to the same Redis cluster, so each call returns the memory info for all cluster nodes; with N flusher processes this issues N× the INFO round-trips per submit and sums N copies of the same used/available values (the ratio is unchanged but the work is redundant). Similarly `record_stored_segments()` is called per buffer. Querying memory info once (e.g. on a single buffer) is sufficient.

findings.title: Docstring claims one process per shard, but the default CLI setting is a single process
findings.body: The class docstring says "Creates one process per shard for parallel processing", but the number of processes is `min(max_processes, len(assigned_shards))`, and the `--flusher-processes` CLI option defaults to 1, so in the default configuration a single process handles all shards. The docstring should describe the actual sharding (shards are round-robin assigned to up to `max_processes` processes) and mention the `max_processes` parameter.

findings.title: No test covers shard-to-process assignment correctness or the multi-process restart path
findings.body: `test_flusher_processes_limit` only checks process counts and that the total number of mapped shards equals 4. It does not assert that shards are disjoint across processes or balanced (e.g. process 0 -> [0, 2], process 1 -> [1, 3]), and nothing exercises `_ensure_processes_alive` restarting one of several processes (per-index restart counters, per-index healthy_since/backpressure values, killing the old process). Given the isinstance bug in the kill path, a test that drives a process into the unhealthy state and verifies the old one is gone would have caught it.
